missionPremise: The kit gives .pill and .prov display: inline-flex and .state and .metric display: flex, so an author declaration of equal or greater weight beats the user-agent [hidden] rule and el.hidden = true is inert on them. Sources: web/shell.css lines 104, 122, 259 and 296 at base 23154be; the G-76 to G-79 close at _inbox/2026-08-18_g76_g79_fixture_city_and_type.md, which records the shipped defect (an amber Partial pill beside 'no meeting packet has been read') and names the root fix as one [hidden] rule in shell.css; and the comment block at web/app.js lines 39 to 53, which documents the same thing from the other side. The card's own reading of the defect was confirmed at source, not taken on trust: the two per-component patches were found at shell.css:704 and shell.css:732, and the four component display declarations were read directly.
completionPredicate: A stranger can check this without me. (1) web/shell.css contains exactly one rule selecting the bare hidden attribute, it declares display: none !important, it is not inside an at-rule, and no other rule in the file declares an important display. (2) .stage[hidden] and .stage-esc[hidden] are gone. (3) In a browser, a hidden .pill, .prov, .state and .metric each compute display: none while their non-hidden siblings compute inline-flex, inline-flex, flex and flex, and a component display rule declared after the global rule does not change that. (4) Nothing without the attribute computes none. (5) npm test is green including every test this lane did not write, and the new guard has been watched fail against a mutated real file. All five hold and are evidenced below.
scopeBasis: The card grants web/shell.css and a new test file, and fences off web/index.html, web/app.js, web/sc-kit.css and the rest of src/ because the G-80 lane owns them this wave. Everything outside that fence is deliberately untouched, including the now-redundant show() helper in app.js, which the card explicitly says to leave. One exception was forced and is recorded in full under boundaryCrossing: src/ui.test.mjs asserted the literal text of a patch this card retires, so the card's build instruction and its ownership fence could not both be honoured. The narrowest crossing that keeps every other instruction was taken rather than either leaving a red test or leaving the patch in place.
ruleLocation: web/shell.css line 51, unconditional, placed immediately after the base reset and before the type block
specificityReasoning: An attribute selector scores (0,1,0) and so does a class, so [hidden] and .pill tie and source order decides, which is why the user-agent rule loses today. Raising selector weight only moves the tie somewhere else: [hidden][hidden] is (0,2,0), which beats one class but ties .lens.on and .shell-nav.open and loses to any future rule carrying three simple selectors, and html [hidden] at (0,1,1) loses to any two-class rule. Placing the rule last in the file is the same bet in different clothing, because the next component rule can be appended after it. Every one of those forms is a bet on where the next rule lands, and this card exists precisely because that bet kept being lost. An important author declaration sits in the important-author cascade origin, which outranks every normal author declaration regardless of specificity, regardless of position in the file, and regardless of a normal inline style attribute, so the rule holds without knowing anything about the rest of the stylesheet. That is the property the card asked for, and it was verified by measurement, not by argument: a component rule declared AFTER the global rule still loses.
exclusionSet: hidden="until-found" is carved out because the user-agent sheet gives that value content-visibility: hidden rather than display: none. Forcing display: none on it would change platform semantics rather than restore them. Measured zero occurrences of until-found in web/ and src/ at base 23154be, so the carve-out is inert today and is documented as such in the rule's comment. It is also the only carve-out the guard permits; any other :not() on the global rule fails the test as narrowed-global.

the rule placed last in the file — correctness depends on nobody appending a component rule after it
